agent_position: Move only the site's lease clock with both doubles (option B); leave the storefronts on wall time, since they act on authority-recorded instants and a future end is a truncation the site enforces
owner_disposition: One lane time shared by every party (L1): storefronts, site, registry, doubles, the buyer CLI and the harness's signing clients each move their whole perception of time together, set from the e2e test through an API; the buyer moves in this change. The goal is fully deterministic e2e verification of rate deals, not watchdogs paused and records back-dated; absolute time is irrelevant at best and harmful at worst when the test drives time
summary: Lane time spans every party, buyer included, instead of the site's lease clock alone

agent_position: P1 with a boolean setting named for 'perceived time' and no livemode coupling: a refusal or warning keyed to livemode protects only payments-configured parties while suggesting all are protected
owner_disposition: P1, softened: the production image necessarily carries the control, so the injected clock is off by default and production configuration simply omits the override; the setting is time.source = "wall" | "injected"; the status endpoint reports that time is injected and its current injected value; a party warns when injected time is enabled beside payments livemode = true
summary: Injected time as time.source, reported with its value on status, warned beside livemode

agent_position: (i): the application supplies every database time, existing DDL defaults stay inert, and the check flags func.now(), CURRENT_TIMESTAMP and datetime('now') outside released migration steps
owner_disposition: (i'): convert only the database times production logic reads (a column a query orders, filters or expires by, or a decision compares); an audit-only created_at/updated_at nothing reads keeps its SQL default, the check covers Python reads only, and store integration tests under injected time assert the read columns. Many tables carry a created_at that is hard to supply from the application and affects no test, so 'SQL never computes time' is not promoted
summary: Database times converted only where production logic reads them
